en: They were afraid and made no answer.
Could they turn aside Manas's words?
Once he had ordered, 'Drive them!'
Could the companions fail to drive them?
Ajybay of Khan Argyn
And Chubak of Akbaltay,
'Drive them all here!' they said,
As they passed the order.
Moving sideways like a swift horse,
Zhamgyrchy of the Eshtek,
Folding his hands and bowing,
Came to Manas and began to speak,
Speaking softly and deliberately:
Here are the Nogay people with their sovereign,
Here is the dark pit that has been dug;
Here is the brine to boil us in.
If you would bind us, here are our hands;
If you would drive us, here is the road;
If you would slaughter, here we are!
Through ridges with towering passes,
We came shooting argali and eating them.
'While lion Manas is among us,
With the renowned land of Beijing
Let us exchange shots,' we said, and came.
'The Chinese with red tassels
He will slaughter for us,' we said, and came.
Beijing, beyond Chalyar’s reach,
He will bring within our measure,' we said, and came.
'Beijing, untouched by His Holiness,
If hero Manas finds the means,
He will conquer for us,' we said, and came.
With a hemp sash and broad boots,
Kongurbay, khan of the monks,
That fearsome fellow, at full length,
He will lay out for us,' we said, and came.
'The shot-proof garments Kanykey made
Let us put on,' we said, and came.
'The Kalmyks dwelling in Khangay,
While Khan Manas is among us,
Let us attack,' we said, and came.
'The teeming people in the east,
Let us engage in conflict,' we said, and came.
'While peerless Manas is among us,
The swarming Chinese,
Let us exchange shots with them,' we said, and came.
'For the warrior to wear far from home,
Let us be a coat,' we said, and came.
'If he sets out on a distant journey,
Let us be his army,' we said, and came.”
Then Manas said, “Agreed!
What Zhamgyrchy has said
Is counsel for us all.”
Giving six swift horses,
Giving a letter small as a palm,
“Let my elder Koshoy come,
Of Kakanchyn's Beijing,
Let him see the great turmoil!
Has it not been spoken of?
The twelve Muslim khans,
Let him drive them all here.
Let the leopard turn his head this way.
My sacred elder,
The Muslims' red banner,
Against the massed Chinese,
Tell him to hold it for us.
After my elder Koshoy,
Aykhojo of Andijan,
Let him heed these words of mine:
For all these people here,
Tell him to serve as imam.
In the sky the blue-mottled clouds were gray;
Hero Er Töshtük of Eleman—
We were friends for the world to come.
Let no mistaken message be sent;
Hero Er Töshtük of Eleman
Must not be left out of this journey.
Whoever travels without ritual washing,
Fold him at the waist and crush him!
Whoever speaks in protest,
I shall slaughter and spill his blood,
Gathering his four kinds of livestock.
If he refuses to obey me,
I shall slaughter him before his appointed hour.
Whoever gives a retort,
I shall seize him by the back,
Have him dragged along the road
And torn apart by great dogs.
Muslims, if this is so,
What I have said is wise counsel.
From this Beijing before us,
Whoever holds back is an infidel, I say.
Let him not open a path into the hills;
Let the Muslims who hear this
Not flee to their separate homes.
Forty companions, born as lions,
You lived at ease in Talas;
The khans who turned back from Beijing
You drove here under guard.
Let them not scout a path through the hills,
The Muslims, their death-hour come,
Let them not disobey and meet their deaths!”
With six swift horses,
And a letter the size of a palm,
He took the twisted brass spear,
Grasped its end and swung it round.
He mounted him on Zhelmaian,
His felt cap like a yurt's roof covering,
And sent the hero Shuutu.
The messenger went with the news;
Before Khan Koshoy
He laid down the letter.
Once the letter was given to Koshoy,
Koshoy read the letter then,
Read it swiftly without turning aside,
And, reading, shouted aloud:
“You twelve Muslim khans,
Come, all of you!” he called.
Hearing this, the Muslims
All came in excitement.
“We shall go to Beijing!”
They all cried, equally stirred.
“I shall make the journey to Beijing!
While valiant Manas is with us,
A waist like a sheath, a face like the moon—
I shall take a wife from Beijing!”
Many rejoiced with such thoughts.
“To Beijing, beyond even a holy one's reach,
He will drive us and get us killed,
March us on a distant journey,
Bind us, drive us, and get us killed!”
Many more were distressed at this.
Great throughout the whole wide world,
Aykhozho of Andijan
Had come to serve the faith.
Koshoy and the hero Er Toshtuk,
The khan, came together.
The Muslims who had stayed behind
Now all came along.
It was where they counted everyone,
Where the forty companions divided the guests.
All the companions made ready,
Preparing to receive their guests.
At the sight of the forty companions,
Those who arrived were amazed.
Unable to withstand their imposing presence,
Their minds were bewildered.
If you looked at the forty companions,
They wore swords of gold;
The heroes, slender as awns,
Held their spears steady.
Among the horses, the pied-headed racers;
Almambet and Chubak, their mounts a match,
With the hero Bakai in their midst,
All together, lions.
When they counted the people,
The Muslims who had come from Kokand,
When they entered the people in writing,
The army numbered twelve great hosts.
Azizkhan's son Almambet
Had also pitched a thousand yurts.
Akbaltay's son Chubak
Had also pitched a thousand yurts.
Ajybai and Bakai, the two khans,
Pitched a thousand yurts.
The leopard named Kazan,
Their khan, pitched a thousand yurts.
Each of the forty companions,
Every one, pitched a thousand yurts.
After entering the people in writing,
After reckoning the journey,
Almambet and Chubak took the lead
And divided the people among them.
They slaughtered mares to entertain their guests;
Those with the means slaughtered camels.
They crunched sugar like snow,
Sipped their black tea,
And drank spirits to quench their thirst.
The twelve Muslim khans
Had all flocked to Talas.
The great army bound for Beijing
Was fed for eighty days.
The hilltops were broad green meadows;
They had ranged across those green meadows.
Yraman's son Yrchy,
And Baabedin's son Baychoro—
No guests were left for them.
Yraman's son Yrchy,
And Baabedin's son Baychoro,
When no guests were left for them,
“Rather than live in this world,
Let us die!” they thought.
“If there is fairness, let us
Have our guests!” they thought.
“If there is no fairness,
Here in Talas itself,
Without mercy, a great commotion
Let us raise!” they thought.
Finding words in a sudden crisis,
Finding a path in the dark,
The wise leopard Bakai
Saw their mood from afar.
From every camp, a hundred guests
He levied and reassigned.
For those two indignant men,
Khan Bakai of great authority
Now found guests.
The appointed time had come,
For Beijing in Kakanchyn:
It was time to set out.
Your dear sister-in-law Kanykei
Had every piece of equipment
Made ready, had she not?
Impenetrable to bullets when worn in battle,
Every piece of clothing
She had prepared, had she not?
She sent word to her people:
“My little handful of Muslims,
May no stray bullet strike you!
‘Blackening, burning embers,’ they say;
‘Thick-flying bullets in Beijing,’ they say;
‘Pits dug ready,’ they say;
‘Great Beijing, land of unbelievers,
Is a harsh and perilous road,’ they say.
Muslims going to Beijing,
Take the coats I give as gifts;
Take the hand of my generous champion khan!
To the hero who thrusts a spear,
I shall give a coat no spear can pierce.
To the marksman entering a firefight,
I shall show that he is a leader;
Where no musket ball can enter,
I shall clothe him in a coat of mail.
Let no head be cut off at the throat.
Saying, ‘I went under compulsion,’
Let no grievance against us remain with you.
Crying out along the way,
Let the Muslims, a mere handful,
Not die of hunger.”
Every implement of Kanykey's was known;
Everything she had was accounted for.
The armor to wear in a firefight
Hung in Kanykey's white court yurt.
The Muslims to go on the campaign
Were recorded in Almambet's list.
Yesterday, Almambet, Azizkan's son,
Had been a solidly built fortress,
Over illustrious Beijing
Had been khan for twenty-one years.
The golden throne in Beijing—
Had not Almambet sat upon it before coming?
Against his skin, a white camel-wool shirt—
Had he not come wearing it?
Every skill of the Chinese—
Had he not come knowing it?
